subject: Anthropic priced at $83, and index funds buy Nov 30
bodyMarkdown:
Anthropic priced its IPO at 83 US dollars a share last night, above the 70 to 78 range it had been marketing, and it starts trading on the Nasdaq this morning under the ticker ANT. If you hold a broad index fund that covers the world outside Canada, you are about to own a piece of this whether you looked at the prospectus or not, and the dates for that are already on the calendar.

## What got priced last night

The CBC reported that 83 dollars values Anthropic at roughly 1.51 trillion US dollars once you count unvested employee options and other promised shares, and closer to 1.1 trillion on the shares that actually exist today. The company sold about 980 million shares after lifting the deal from the 825 million it had planned, raising about 81.3 billion before the underwriters' option on another 147 million shares. That makes it the largest offering ever done, ahead of the roughly 75 billion SpaceX raised in June. Most of those shares came from the company rather than from existing holders, which means most of the money lands on the balance sheet instead of in someone's brokerage account. A deal that prices above its own range and gets upsized on the way is a deal where the books were covered days ago.

## The money behind the money

Here is the part I would read twice. Dealroom's summary of the draft S-1 put first half revenue at 16.3 billion US dollars against a net loss of 80.7 billion, with about 72 billion of that loss being non cash charges tied to the instruments Anthropic issued to raise money in the first place. Strip those out and the operating loss for the half was 693 million on 16.3 billion of revenue, which is a different company than the headline suggests. Several accounts of last night's pricing also describe a concurrent 26 billion private placement of non voting shares at the same 83 dollars, taken up by strategic partners including Nvidia, Google, Microsoft and Broadcom. The numbers in those reports do not agree with each other yet, so I am waiting on the final prospectus. If it holds, the suppliers and the cloud landlords just helped fund their own customer.

## When it shows up in your index fund

This is the mechanical part, and it is the part that touches an ordinary Canadian portfolio. MSCI said on November 12 that Anthropic is on track for early inclusion in its Global Standard indexes, with an expected date of November 30. CNBC reported that FTSE Russell will not add it until the open on December 14. The Nasdaq 100 can take a new listing after its fifteenth trading day if it ranks inside the top 40 by market value, and Morningstar figures a trillion dollar company clears that. The S&P 500 is the holdout, since it wants 12 months of trading history, so do not expect it there before late 2027. Morningstar also notes the free float is only about 6 per cent, so index funds will be buying a sliver of a very large company on fixed dates.

## The takeaway

I would not buy anything on its first morning of trading, and that goes double for a company whose float is 6 per cent. The dates to mark are November 30 and December 14, because passive money has to buy on those days at whatever price the market has set, and a thin float plus forced buyers is how you get a price that has nothing to do with the business. If you want to judge the business, wait for the first quarterly report that comes with an auditor and a 10-Q rather than a draft prospectus. And keep the 72 billion of non cash charges in mind when the first profitability headline shows up, in either direction.
